# Talk to ChatGPT by voice on your phone while cooking or driving

> **In short:** With the ChatGPT phone app you can have a spoken conversation with the assistant — ask out loud, hear the answer, follow up — hands-free. Setup takes about a minute; some of the most natural-sounding voices may need a paid plan.

By the end of this guide you'll have ChatGPT's voice mode working on your phone, ready to chat with you out loud while your hands are busy. This is for anyone who wants a hands-free way to brainstorm, settle a small argument, plan dinner, or just keep a conversation going without staring at a screen.

## Before you start
- **An iPhone or Android phone** with the free ChatGPT app installed (App Store on iPhone, Google Play on Android). Tablet works too.
- **A ChatGPT account** — the free plan is enough to try voice mode, and sign-up takes about two minutes with any email address.
- **About five minutes** total: two for install and sign-in, three for your first conversation.
- **A calm-ish first moment.** Test voice mode somewhere quiet first (a kitchen counter, a parked car, a quiet room). Once you know it works, you can take it anywhere.

## Step 1 — Install the ChatGPT app
Open your phone's app store — the **App Store** on iPhone, **Google Play** on Android — and search for "ChatGPT". The official app is published by OpenAI and shows a black square icon with a white, interlocking flower-like logo. Tap **Install** or **Get**, then wait for the download to finish.

If the store search is crowded with lookalikes, ignore anything that asks for payment upfront or has a different publisher name. The official one is free and clearly labeled "OpenAI" as the developer.

You'll know it worked when you see the black ChatGPT icon on your home screen and tapping it opens a screen that says "Welcome to ChatGPT."

💬 Example: search term to copy — `ChatGPT`

## Step 2 — Sign in or create a free account
When the app opens, you'll see a **Sign up** button and a **Log in** link at the bottom. If you already have a ChatGPT account, tap Log in and enter your email and password. If not, tap Sign up — you'll need an email address you can check (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, or any other works) plus your name and birthday.

Sign-up usually sends a verification code to your email. After that, you land directly on the free plan. The free plan covers basic voice mode; the most natural-sounding voices and longer voice sessions may need a paid plan like ChatGPT Plus — we'll get to that distinction in a moment.

You'll know it worked when the screen shows "How can I help today?" with a message box at the bottom.

💬 Example: sign-up email — any address you check regularly; the verification code arrives in your inbox within a minute.

## Step 3 — Tap the microphone icon to start voice mode
At the bottom of the chat screen, next to the text box, look for a **microphone icon** 🎤 — or sometimes a **headphones** or **sound-wave** icon. Tap it once. The screen changes: the keyboard slides away and a circular animation appears, usually labeled "Listening…" with a pulsing dot in the middle.

If you can't spot a microphone on the main screen, look inside a small **"⋯"** or **"+"** button near the message box — some app versions tuck voice there. On Android it sometimes lives one tap deeper than on iPhone, so don't panic if it takes a second to find.

You'll know it worked when the screen shows a clear listening indicator and the text box is replaced by a voice prompt.

💬 Example: just tap the mic once and wait for the listening circle — you don't need to press and hold the button.

## Step 4 — Ask your first spoken question
Once you see the listening indicator, talk in a normal voice, as if a friend were sitting across from you. Speak **one clear sentence at a time**, then pause for a moment. The app shows your words as text on the screen as it hears them, so you can check it understood you. When you stop talking, ChatGPT responds out loud through your phone's speaker.

If you're in a noisy kitchen, hold the phone a little closer to your mouth or step away from the blender. If you're in the car, use Bluetooth or a phone mount so you don't need to pick the device up. Keep your eyes where they need to be — on the road, on the cutting board — and let your ears do the work.

You'll know it worked when you hear ChatGPT's spoken answer come back through the speaker within a couple of seconds, in a voice that sounds like a real person rather than a robot.

💬 Example: *"I'm making dinner with chicken, rice, and broccoli. What sauce can I whip up in ten minutes with stuff I probably already have?"*

## Step 5 — Keep the conversation going naturally
Voice mode works like a real chat — you can interrupt, ask follow-ups, or change direction mid-answer. If ChatGPT starts rambling, just say **"shorter please"** or **"give me the top three."** If you want to switch topics entirely, just ask the new question; you don't need to say "new topic" first.

You can mute the speaker any time by tapping the speaker icon mid-conversation, or end the chat with the **X** or **End** button. When you end, voice mode stops listening and the regular text box returns. Your spoken conversation is automatically saved as text in your chat history, so you can scroll back later or copy a recipe into your notes.

You'll know it worked when you can fire off three or four follow-up questions in a row without tapping anything except maybe the mic once at the start.

💬 Example: follow-ups — *"Make it spicy."* → *"Do I have everything for that?"* → *"Okay, last step by step while I cook."*

## Step 6 — Change the voice or stop the session
To swap the voice, look for a **settings gear ⚙** or a small **voice icon** while you're in voice mode — a panel usually slides up with several voice options, each with a different tone or accent. Tap any of them to hear a short sample, then pick the one that sounds most natural to your ear. The voice you choose sticks as your default for future chats.

To finish, tap **End** or the **X** button. The screen goes back to normal chat mode, and your conversation appears in the sidebar with all the spoken words saved as text. Next time you want hands-free, open any chat and tap the mic again — it remembers your chosen voice.

You'll know it worked when the next voice session greets you in the voice you picked last time.

💬 Example: voice names vary by region and update over time — try two or three for a few seconds each and trust the one that feels easiest to listen to for a long chat.

## Common mistakes
- **Talking before the listening indicator appears.** The app needs that half-second to start capturing audio cleanly. Wait for the pulsing circle or "Listening…" text, then speak — otherwise the first word or two often gets cut off.
- **Expecting ChatGPT to browse live recipe sites or traffic reports on command.** Voice mode can use general knowledge and recent training data, but it can't reliably pull from a live URL or a paywalled article while you're chatting. If the answer feels vague, finish what you're doing first, then ask for sources in text mode.
- **Looking at the screen while driving.** Voice mode is hands-free for talking and ears-free for listening, but your eyes still need to stay on the road. For anything visual — long answers, lists, links — pull over first, or hand the mic to a passenger and let them drive.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You're chopping vegetables with wet hands and need to convert cups to grams — just ask out loud. You're folding laundry and want a podcast-style recap of the news — voice mode can walk you through it while your hands stay busy.
- **For your business or work:** On a long drive between meetings, you can brainstorm ideas, talk through a presentation outline, or rehearse what you'll say to a client. Save anything sensitive for text mode, where you can review and edit before sending.
- **If you're just getting started:** Try the simplest possible thing first — ask it the time in another city, or to tell you a knock-knock joke. That removes the pressure and shows you how natural the back-and-forth feels before you bring it into the kitchen or the car.

## Try it now
Open the ChatGPT app, tap the microphone once, and ask: *"I'm about to cook with [whatever's in your fridge right now]. What can I make in twenty minutes?"* Then just listen, follow up, and let your hands stay where they're needed.
